visual_appeal: Reduce competing hero accents: retain the green state rail and portrait ring, but lower the full bar's saturation approximately 15% and make its internal tick marks 20% opacity. The large green rectangle currently competes with the recommended character's name.

Use one 14 px body treatment and one 12 px secondary treatment across the main window. The current mixture of bold metadata, gold headings, segmented bars and outlined chips makes nearly every element demand attention.
Give the hero's plan strip 12 px horizontal padding and at least 8 px vertical padding; its contents currently read as a tightly packed toolbar rather than a considered recommendation.
play_next_clarity: Make the repair action visibly conditional: change step 1 to 'Before switching: Le Jette, hearth to an inn' and step 2 to 'Play Le Dette'. Keep the character names in their existing class colours.
Move 'Then Le Bankken, full in 19h' onto a separate, subordinate line below the numbered actions. It currently introduces a third character into the same narrow decision strip.
Replace 'Full since 1d 16h ago' with 'Full for 1d 16h'. Put 'Rest beyond the cap is wasted' on its own 12 px amber line rather than appending another bold clause to the success message.
state_colours: For red characters, explicitly qualify the estimate: 'Full in 31d 14h outside an inn'. Repeat that qualifier in the timeline tooltip and compact tooltip; the enormous red ETA currently appears directly comparable to inn-resting estimates without explanation.

Use the same state hues for rails, portrait outlines, bars and chips, with lighter text variants only where required for contrast. In particular, bring the dark red timeline lane closer to the roster's clearly legible warning red.

In compact mode, add a tooltip that names each pip's character and state, and provide at least 4 px separation between state groups. The adjacent orange pips are otherwise an indistinguishable cluster.
character_identity: On the character card, align the speech bubble, character name, metadata and state chip to a shared left edge at 76 px in the shown crop. The current 76–87 px offsets look accidental.
Move the card's name block approximately 24 px upward, reducing the large gap below the speech bubble. Preserve the portrait's size and its settled class-badge treatment.

Separate the two tidbit concepts currently combined as 'HEARTH · LOGGED OUT': use 'HEARTH' above its destination, and put the logout location in the rest-summary line. Identical locations in this fixture conceal the ambiguity.
default_theme: Darken the scenic hero background with a uniform black overlay around 45% opacity. Its brightest rocks sit behind metadata and weaken the otherwise deliberate bronze framing.
Use a dark brown track such as #17130E rather than pure black for unfilled default-theme bars, with a 1 px #665039 border. The current empty tracks look cut out of the warm panel.
Reserve the lighter bronze button treatment for the primary action. Make Compact, Unlink and the account selector visibly secondary with a darker fill and equal 22 px heights.
elvui_wc3_fit: The frame and blue buttons belong beside the supplied host windows, but the typography does not yet match as closely. Apply the host's configured ElvUI font to body text and controls rather than retaining the addon’s conspicuously serif-heavy treatment.
Match the host's red close-button dimensions and inset consistently across the main window, character card and alerts; the tiny alert crosses currently look like a separate control family.

Style the addon's options using the host's actual checkbox, radio and slider treatments. The flat grey checkbox blocks and pale slider thumb in the render do not resemble the supplied yellow-filled host controls.
Give Roster and Timeline explicit 22 px tab targets with a restrained selected background and gold underline. Their current tiny text links feel less finished than the surrounding WC3 controls.
alerts_ux: Shorten the logout banner's primary instruction to 'Cancel logout and hearth to an inn'. Use the next line for 'Hearth: Feathermoon Stronghold', avoiding the repeated inn instruction across title and body.
Give dismiss and settings controls separate, consistent 22 × 22 px hit areas with at least 6 px between them. Keep the dismissal cross visually distinct from the nearby frame ornament.
Use a genuine moon symbol for the Esc card and its mover. The shown scroll-like icon does not read as a moon and weakens the intended distinction from the other warnings.
Add a visible 'Attached to Esc menu' badge and a small anchor indicator to the Esc mover. Keep 'Drag to detach' below it so the attachment behavior is understandable before the player moves it.
In the toast, reduce the trigger line's weight and increase its contrast to approximately #D9AD65. Keep 'Play Le Dette' as the sole 15 px primary line.
readability: Increase roster metadata and ETA text to at least 13 px at the shown 1:1 size, and use 14 px for actionable advice. Do not depend on the optional 115% setting to make routine information comfortable.

Show the calendar ETA for every roster row, not only the nearly-full row: use a second line such as 'Thu 3 Dec, 05:00' under 'Full in 9d'. Increase row height from roughly 58 px to 66 px if necessary.
Increase the timeline's after-48-hour column to approximately 120 px and use two intentional lines: 'Wed 2 Dec' and '01:36'. Remove the repeated 'Full' prefix from every lane.
Increase options-row spacing to 26 px and place long explanations beneath their labels in 12 px muted text. The current window-and-display checklist is visually cramped.
Replace the cryptic account label '#3' with 'Account 3', and provide the actual account alias in its tooltip.
layout_polish: Resolve the hero's right-column alignment: center the numeric value, LEVELS BANKED label and FULL chip on one vertical axis, and reserve a fixed 112 px column for that group.
Split the plan into an action area and a right-aligned View details button with a fixed 12 px gutter. Do not squeeze the runner-up into the remaining space between them.
Preserve roster ordering when switching to Timeline, or explicitly label the alternate sort 'By time to full'. Jacques Hammer changes position between views without a visible explanation.
Increase the options panel's bottom padding to 20 px and separate the About copy from the alert settings with a 1 px divider and 12 px gap. It currently looks appended to the last checkbox section.
Use a consistent 12 px internal gutter for the character card's summary box and tidbit box; their text and bar currently start on slightly different vertical guides.
delight: Make the speech feel character-specific: retain the short first line, then use a class or location-aware second line rather than generic comfort copy. Keep both within the existing bubble instead of enlarging the card.
On a new recommended character, use a restrained 250–350 ms gold edge sweep on the hero only, disabled by Reduce motion. Avoid animating the whole roster or adding persistent glow.
When dismissing an alert, briefly show 'Dismissed for this session' in the same footprint for about 1.5 seconds. This supplies quiet confirmation without introducing a popup.
Give the compact strip a clear hover state around the entire clickable area, not just its individual icons, so the miniature presentation feels intentional rather than like exposed status tokens.

overall_notes: A substantial improvement over the real baseline: the recommendation has stronger hierarchy, the current-character strip is coherent, and the character card is much less wasteful. The WC3 framing and blue controls convincingly establish the intended environment. This is still not demanding-user approval territory. Dense small typography, a congested action strip, inconsistent information density between views, and underqualified outside-rest-area estimates remain material issues. The default theme is attractive but slightly overdecorated; the ElvUI mode needs closer control and font integration rather than more ornament. The simulator's missing 3D rendering and narrower fonts are not counted as defects, and the settled portrait and state-colour rules are respected.
